result.rule: When the description states that a consequence (such as a fine) applies to a party only if a required action is not completed within a stated time period, and the process continues afterwards: Model an exclusive gateway at the point where the deadline outcome is decided, with one labeled outgoing sequence flow for the not-completed case and one for the completed case. On the not-completed branch, model the consequence as a task (for example a service task) that applies it, not as a terminal end event. Then join the branch back into the normal flow, so the process continues afterwards. Use a timer intermediate event for the time period only if the description states the period as a wait to be awaited, and do not replace the decision with it.

When the description says a participant may postpone an activity when they have another task to handle, so the activity is delayed and not always performed at its first opportunity: Model the postponement as its own task on a branch that leaves an exclusive gateway. The gateway tests whether the participant has another pending task. One outgoing flow leads to the postponement task, which returns to the same test (or to a point before the postponed activity is retried). The other flow continues the normal path to the postponed activity. Do not omit the postponement branch, and do not replace the postponement with a plain skip or an unconditional flow.

When the description states that a branch or outcome ends with a closing or recording action performed by a participant, such as closing an item or making a booking, before the process outcome is reached: Model each such stated action as a task on that branch, placed after the decision or preceding step and before the end event of that outcome. Do not omit the action or connect the decision directly to the end event.

When the description says that after an exclusive check of whether an available quantity or set of items is sufficient, a shortfall must be covered by a stated obtaining action (for example, acquiring what is still needed) before the process goes on: After the exclusive decision that checks sufficiency, add a task on the insufficient branch that performs the stated obtaining action, named after the description's wording. Route that task into the same continuation the sufficient branch reaches, so the shortfall is handled explicitly before the process proceeds. Do not leave the insufficient branch as a bare sequence flow to the join.

result.rule: When the description says that an external party or a later event will act at a time that is not fixed in advance (for example, they arrive at a random time) and that a following activity can only start after that moment: Model the waiting period as an intermediate catch event placed immediately before the activity that depends on it, and do not represent the wait by a task or by the dependent activity itself.

When the description says that the party sends a request or material to another party and then has to wait for that party's reply, confirmation or status before it continues: Model the send as a send activity, and model the wait for the reply as an explicit receive activity placed directly after it and before the next activity or decision that depends on the reply. Do not connect the send activity directly to the later step, and do not drop the wait from the flow.

When the description says the process waits until a group of people has replied or until a set of items has been collected before the next decision or step: Model that wait as an intermediate catch event placed after the request task and before the gateway or activity that uses the collected replies or items, so the waiting step is explicit in the flow rather than merged into the request or decision.

When the description says a request is sent to a party and a follow-up is set in the meantime, and the process then waits for either a reply or a timed deadline, so the path depends on which occurs first: Model the wait as an event-based gateway. Give the awaited reply its own intermediate catch event, and give the timed follow-up its own intermediate timer catch event. Connect the timer catch event with a direct sequence flow to the activity the description says follows the missed deadline. Do not insert another gateway or an extra wait between the timer event and that activity, and do not route the timer branch into an unrelated activity or a new end event.
